description: E4 gold claims for the figure check (D36). Written by looking at each figure as the parser cropped it; labels are what the image shows. 'expected' is the verdict a correct checker gives. A 'not_shown' claim is about something neither the image nor the caption states.

claims.claim: The collapsed tree reaches a higher F1 than tree traversal at a context length of 1000.
Tree traversal outperforms the collapsed tree at every context length.
claims.note: collapsed tree is higher from 500 to 2000

claims.claim: The collapsed tree's F1 peaks at a context length of about 2000, around 59, and then declines.
The collapsed tree's F1 keeps increasing up to a context length of 2500.
In this figure, GPT-4 is the model that reads the retrieved context.
claims.note: the image and the caption name no reader model

claims.claim: Prompt and completion tokens grow roughly linearly with document length on all three datasets.
On NarrativeQA, even the longest documents use fewer than 100,000 prompt and completion tokens.
Building the tree for QASPER costs less money than for QuALITY.
claims.note: no cost in money is shown

claims.claim: Building the tree for a document of about 78,000 tokens takes about 1,750 seconds.
Build time decreases steadily as document length grows.
Build time drops between documents of about 29,000 and 42,000 tokens.
On QuALITY, most retrieved nodes come from layer 0 for all three retrievers.
On NarrativeQA, DPR retrieves a larger share of layer-0 nodes than SBERT.
On NarrativeQA, DPR retrieves a larger share of layer-1 nodes than SBERT and BM25.
On QASPER, more than 30% of retrieved nodes come from layer 2.
The figure shows text chunks being clustered and each cluster summarized by an LLM to form a tree layer.
A node stores an index, its child nodes, a summary text and a text embedding.
The RAPTOR tree drawn in the figure has three nodes in its root layer.
RAPTOR's clustering step uses Gaussian mixture models.
claims.note: the diagram does not say which clustering

claims.claim: The figure shows two ways to form queries: implicit, by masking, and explicit, by question generation.
In the figure, the explicit questions are generated by a BM25 retriever.
FLARE achieves the highest score on all five datasets.
On 2WikiMultihopQA, FLARE scores 51.0 against 28.2 without retrieval.
On StrategyQA, single-time retrieval outperforms no retrieval.
On WikiAsp, FLARE scores 58.4.
On ASQA, previous-window retrieval scores slightly below single-time retrieval.
On 2WikiMultihopQA, performance rises from 28.2 with no retrieval to 51.0 when every step retrieves.
StrategyQA performance increases steadily as the share of steps with retrieval goes from 0 to 100%.
StrategyQA peaks at 77.3 when about 40% of the steps retrieve.
The multi-step approach takes the most time per query, close to 9.
Adaptive-RAG reaches an F1 close to the multi-step approach in well under half its time per query.
No Retrieval achieves a higher F1 than Adaptive Retrieval.
Adaptive-RAG is the fastest of the methods shown.
claims.note: No Retrieval, Adaptive Retrieval and Single-step are faster

claims.claim: In the adaptive approach, a classifier routes straightforward, simple and complex queries to different strategies.
In the multi-step approach panel, the complex query is answered after a single retrieval step.
The single-step approach has the lowest F1 of the methods shown, about 47.
No Retrieval takes more time per query than the multi-step approach.

figures.kind: three panels: a table image, line plots

claims.claim: In the ablation, removing the retriever lowers PQA accuracy from 45.5 to 43.6.
Increasing the weight for IsSupport increases Mauve.
Precision rises as the IsSupport weight goes from 0 to 1 and then stays flat.
Removing the critic lowers the AS em score to 28.6.

figures.kind: line plots and a small table

claims.claim: PopQA performance increases as the number of training examples grows to 150k.
PubHealth performance is highest at 150k training examples.
In the human evaluation, IsRel reaches 95.0 on PopQA.
The training examples were annotated by GPT-4.
Self-CRAG stays above Self-RAG at every level of retrieval accuracy shown.
As retrieval accuracy drops from 69.8 to 10, Self-RAG's generation accuracy falls from about 55 to about 33.
Self-CRAG falls below the no-retrieval line when retrieval accuracy is low.
